snippet.title: Tom Cruise Nearly Died on this $100 million Box Office Movie
snippet.description:
Tom Cruise is willing to do anything for a role! And sometimes, that even means putting his own life at risk. These movies may have managed to make over $100 million at the box office, but their leading acting had to go to some pretty extreme lengths in order to do it! For example, his co-star Barry Tubb from Top Gun said that Tom came about as close to losing his life on set as he’s ever seen any actor do before! We just hope he managed to stay a little safer while filming for Top Gun: Maverick! Meanwhile, Emily Blunt failed to listen to Tom Cruise’s advice while performing a driving stunt on Edge of Tomorrow, and the star of A Quiet Place and Mary Poppins Returns from the Walt Disney Company actually worried that she have seriously hurt him – or worse! And she isn’t the only co-star of Tom Cruise to have suffered a similar anxiety; comedian Jamie Foxx was also involved in a stunt gone wrong with Tom on the set for Collateral. The Mission: Impossible franchise is equally no stranger to stunts gone wrong for Tom Cruise; in fact, he even broke his ankle while chasing Henry Cavill (best known for the Netflix series the Witcher as well as for playing Superman on the DC Extended Universe) across rooftops for Mission: Impossible - Fallout! Tom Cruise nearly lost his head (literally) while working on The Last Samurai, but it’s a good thing co-star Hiroyuki Sanada was trained so well in martial arts!

snippet.title: The Cast of Asteroid City Talk About Their Experience On Set
snippet.description:
Wes Anderson – according to the cast of Asteroid City – is known for his zany, childlike excitement on set, relishing every minute of his shooting day. His ability to create a welcoming atmosphere brings the actors together, forming close-knit friendships. Wes Anderson encourages interpretation and collaboration, allowing the actors to contribute to their characters. He has a knack for pushing actors past their artistic limits – which is why so many of them come back to work for him. Despite the large cast in Asteroid City, 

Wes Anderson prefers a closed, intimate set where he can direct without raising his voice. The costumes in his movies are meticulously tailored, providing actors with a powerful sense of character. There is a spontaneous and exuberant musical number that had Rupert Friend shaking in his boots performing in front of many seasoned musicians. Rupert Friend learned how to lasso and Jeff Goldblum learned how to maneuver on stilts in a constricting alien costume. The UFO scene required inventive techniques to direct the young actors’ reactions. Scarlett Johansson’s acting skills surprised Jason Schwartzman – him calling her some sort of magician, watching her back like it was the first time he’d seen it. 

Overall, Wes Anderson’s filmmaking process is filled with fun, collaboration, and a touch of magic, creating memorable movies loved by audiences and actors alike. Make sure you stick around until the end of the video to find out just how much chaotic, memorable fun these actors had on set.

snippet.title: The One Big Bang Theory Actress That Played Two Different Roles During The Show's Run
snippet.description:
Who doesn’t love The Big Bang Theory? For a whopping twelve-season run, this beloved sitcom’s lovable cast of characters and hilarious plotlines kept its dedicated fan base hooked and always wanting more. Still, when it comes to a show like The Big Bang Theory, even the plenty of rewatches that its diehard fans are inevitably doing keep folks from catching every single detail the series has to offer. One of these details? Well, that would be when two minor characters were actually played by the same actor. Yes – there’s one guest star on the series who played two entirely different people, and most of the major fans of the series totally missed it. The Big Bang Theory had tons of guest stars over the course of its long run – many of whom were major public figures playing themselves, like legendary comic book writer, Stan Lee, history-making astronaut, Buzz Aldrin, Elon Musk, and Steve Wozniak, while others were well-known actors like Kathy Bates as Mrs.Fowler, Sean Astin as Dr. Greg Pemberton, Judy Greer as Dr. Elizabeth Plimpton, Octavia Spencer as Octavia, and Christopher Lloyd as Theodore. While most of these guest stars made one very memorable appearance, an actor by the name of Molly Morgan managed to make two, and most fans would be surprised to discover that they’re the same person. They are, however, different characters… at least we think. Wait until you see the characters played by the same actor. We have a feeling you’ll be craving a rewatch as much as we are.

snippet.title: Movies You Wouldn't Believe Are Based on True Stories
snippet.description:
Often times the most incredible movies are the ones that are based on true events. Rocky, a classic sports movie about an underdog boxer who gets a shot at the heavyweight championship, is actually based on the real-life story of Chuck Wepner, a boxer who went 15 rounds with Muhammad Ali in 1975. The Blind Side tells the story of Michael Oher, an unhoused boy who is taken in by a wealthy family and given a chance to succeed. The movie follows Michael as he learns to play football and eventually earns a scholarship to play at the University of Mississippi. The Blind Side is a heartwarming story about the power of family, community, and perseverance. Indiana Jones, the iconic adventure movie series, is based on the real-life adventures of archaeologist Roy Chapman Andrews. The movies follow Indiana Jones as he travels the world, searching for ancient artifacts and battling evil forces. While the movies take some liberties with the facts, they are inspired by the real-life exploits of Andrews and other archaeologists who explored the world in the early 20th century. Star Wars, the beloved space opera, may seem like pure fantasy, but it is actually based on a number of real-life inspirations. Creator George Lucas drew on everything from mythology to World War II history to create his epic story of Jedi knights, the Force, and intergalactic battles. The themes of good versus evil, redemption, and the power of hope resonate with audiences around the world, making Star Wars a timeless classic.

Taylor Lautner also struggled when it came to the amount of shirtless scenes that he had to do as Jacob Black starting from the immediate sequel New Moon, especially considering they spent so much time filming in the cold and in the rain! The weather also began to affect Anna Kendrick, who played Bella’s human friend Jessica Stanley. In fact, she even went so far as to say that the entire experience was traumatic! Kellan Lutz was able to make quick friends with Jackson Rathbone and Peter Facinelli, but he agrees with Nikki Reed that there was a lot of drama on set!

snippet.title: Spider-Man & Other Movies That Regret Using CGI
snippet.description:
The use of CGI in movies has become increasingly prevalent in recent years, with filmmakers relying on it to bring their visions to life. However, while CGI and VFX can be powerful tools in the right hands, it can also be a double-edged sword. Many movies have fallen victim to the pitfalls of bad CGI. Movies like Star Wars, Spider-Man, and The Mummy are no exception. One of the biggest criticisms about the Star Wars franchise was its use of CGI – which often distracted from the story rather than enhancing it. The Spider-Man movies have also been criticized – especially when it came to the scene where the Green Goblin attacked the parade. Let me just say, fans were not particularly impressed with what was supposed to be a major fight scene. Directors like Stephen Spielberg even went as far as to say that they wished they had cut out major scenes entirely and relied more heavily on practical effects than anything else. George Lucas, after receiving major criticism for his use of CGI in the Star Wars franchise couldn’t emphasize enough how important it is to ground your film in reality. Of course, these weren’t the only movies to dig themselves into a hole of CGI that didn’t age well – we’ll be talking about all of these movies and more – possibly a few of your favorites might fall under the fire as well. Stick around until the end of the video to find out.

snippet.title: Actors Who Turned Down Harry Potter
snippet.description:
The Harry Potter film series is one of the most successful and beloved franchises in cinematic history, but it might have looked very different if certain actors had accepted roles that were offered to them. Over the course of the eight films, there were several high-profile actors who turned down roles for various reasons. Tilda Swinton was offered the role of Professor Sybill Trelawney, Hugh Grant was offered the role of Gilderoy Lockhart, and Ian McKellen passed on the role of Albus Dumbledore after Richard Harris passed away. Others, like Robin Williams and Kate Winslet, were interested in roles but were ultimately unable to participate due to factors like nationality and scheduling conflicts. These decisions ultimately had significant impacts on the films, as the actors who did accept roles brought their own unique interpretations to the characters. However, it's interesting to consider how the films might have looked and felt if some of these other actors had been involved. In any case, the Harry Potter series remains a beloved classic of modern cinema, and its legacy will continue to inspire and entertain audiences for generations to come, but wouldn’t it be interesting for a completely different recast? I’m still stuck on the idea of Robin Williams as Hagrid! That would be a completely different movie. Which actor would you have liked to see in the Wizarding World? Leave a comment and let me know!

snippet.title: Barry Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
Season 4 of Barry is meant to be the final season! And so, in celebration of this dark comedy series from HBO, we’ll be taking you behind the scenes and showing you what went into the making of Barry! We’ll be discussing the casting of Guillermo del Toro, the director of such classics as Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio for Netflix, and the Shape of Water. Bill Hader’s former SNL costar Paul Rudd also happened to have a bit of say into the soundtrack for season 4, with the Marvel Cinematic Universe star suggesting that Bill Hader look to YouTube for his musical inspirations! Barry is both directed by and starring Bill Hader, who you may also recognize from the Walt Disney Company and Pixar animated classic Inside Out, as well as appearing alongside Pennywise in the horror movie It Chapter Two. snippet.title: Harry Potter Scenes That Actually Used Practical Effects
snippet.description:
The Harry Potter movies, of course, have a fair amount of CGI, but did you know they used a lot of practical effects as well? Let’s take the intense game of Wizard’s Chess in Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone. Do you remember toward s the end when they had to actually be on the life-sized chess pieces and one actually blew up with Ron on it? Yeah, that was fully practical. That entire chess set was built by the production designer and the chess piece that blew up with Ron still on it was designed with a compressed air device inside of it. There are also so many other practically created beings, like the Whomping Willow! The tree was built from the ground up on a hydraulic platform that was controlled by the special effects team. How do you sign up for that job?! Also, all of the flying broomstick scenes were fully practical. The cast actually had to sit on those uncomfortable broomsticks for hours and be flown around the set with wires. You’d think it would be pretty fun, but apparently, they often complained about having sore butts after the scene was over. I think I’d still like to try it out though! Buckbeak the Hippogriff was actually fully practical! Even the scenes where he was flying, it was a fully practical puppet that was controlled by an entire team of puppeteers. They even put feathers on the puppet by hand to make it look more realistic!

snippet.title: Miniature Models Used in Star Wars & Other Movies
snippet.description:
The film industry has been utilizing miniature models to bring their world to life for decades! Some of these miniature sets are so impressive, I would’ve never known they weren’t full-size! Like, did you know that the Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry in every Harry Potter movie was a miniature? Or that most of the sets in the Lord of the Rings trilogy were miniatures as well? Some of the most iconic miniature models ever were in the Star Wars trilogy! Imperial Star Destroyer, anyone? The use of miniatures saves the film crew a ton of money and makes shooting certain scenes much easier. Let’s take Stephen Spielberg’s classic, Jurassic Park, for example. A lot of the dinosaurs were miniatures! Can you imagine how much more difficult it would have been to film the movie if they were working with massive-sized dinosaurs? Also, a ton of scenes in Inception utilized miniatures as well, particularly to bring that iconic zero-gravity fight scene to life. The War Rig in Mad Max: Fury Road was also a miniature and was used in a ton of establishing and wide shots. Can you imagine how difficult the scene would’ve been to film considering it had to be literally lit on fire? Would you have known it was a miniature if I didn’t tell you? Let me know in the comments! There are a ton of miniature models to unpack here, so make sure you stick around until the end of the video!

Demi didn’t like a joke that was made on the show and took to Twitter to call out both Zendaya and Disney Channel. That caused a bit of a rift for a while, but Zendaya ended up empathizing with Demi’s perspective and the two were able to mend some wounds. Not all of these feuds ended up in friendships, with all of the members of The Cheetah Girls still not willing to talk to one another. There’s a lot of tea to spill, so make sure you stick around ‘til the end of the video – you might be surprised about some of these fake on-screen friendships.

snippet.title: Actors Who Turned Down Marvel
snippet.description:
We all tend to think of working with Marvel to be an actor’s dream, and yet these are the actors who decided to turn down the Marvel Cinematic Universe, for one reason or another. Jason Momoa may be best known for his work with the DC Extended Universe as Aquaman, or on the HBO series Game of Thrones, but he could have had a chance to appear in the MCU as Drax the Destroyer in Guardians of the Galaxy! Still, we think that Dave Bautista did a great job in the role anyway. Emily Blunt has worked with the Walt Disney Company on Mary Poppins Returns and Jungle Cruise, but she could have had the opportunity to play Black Widow instead of Scarlet Johansson! Russell Crowe was Bryan Singer’s first choice to play Wolverine, and yet he turned it down because of certain similarities between his previous role in Gladiator. But, fortunately for us, Russell Crowe did recommend Hugh Jackman for the part, or else we wouldn’t be able to see him return for the upcoming Deadpool 3! Tom Cruise has made a name for himself with works like Top Gun: Maverick and Mission: Impossible, but did you know that he nearly took Robert Downey Jr.’s place in the part of Iron Man? Joaquin Phoenix would have made the perfect Doctor Strange were it not for Benedict Cumberbatch suiting the role so well, but we still think that he’s done pretty well for himself working with Todd Phillips on the Joker movie.

snippet.title: Netflix Beef Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
The entire internet is raving about the new dark comedy series on Netflix, Beef! Seriously; we can’t get enough of it, and today, we’ll be taking you behind the scenes to share all of the best easter eggs and trivia that you need to know! Beef stars Steven Yeun, an actor who got his big break on the AMC series The Walking Dead before going on to work on a number of animated projects, like the superhero series Invincible and the Netflix series Tuca & Bertie. This last project is also where you may recognize his co-star Ali Wong from, although she has also appeared as a part of the DC Extended Universe in Birds of Prey, and she’s made several appearances on the adult animation series Big Mouth! Joseph Lee has made several appearances alongside Patrick Stewart in Star Trek: Picard, and appears in Beef playing George! Ashley Park has enjoyed an impressive acting career appearing in multiple projects, from playing Mindy Chen in Emily in Paris, Kimber in Only Murders in the Building, or working with the Walt Disney Company and Pixar on Ratatouille: The TikTok Musical. Justin Min has worked on the podcast series Marvel's Wastelanders: Wolverine, although you may also recognize him from the Umbrella Academy! Beef is a character study inspired by an example of road rage that actually happened to series creator Lee Sung Jin, and there are plenty of other personal touches from the actors throughout the series! Plus, just a bit of inspiration from the HBO series the Sopranos.
